D.comparison: traditional classroom education or other learning modalities

O.outcome_detail: learner satisfaction, usefulness, ease of use, and preference

cells.quote: Most learners reported podcasts to be useful for learning and easy to use. With respect to learning, listeners found podcasts either no different from classroom education or better than traditional lectures.
cells.note: Qualitative synthesis of 24 reaction-outcome articles; no standardized validated reaction tools were used, and comparisons varied across studies.

D.comparison: lectures, traditional training, or no comparison

O.outcome_detail: quiz and examination performance after podcast learning

cells.quote: Nine papers detailed an improvement in test scores when podcasts were utilized, though few studies used a control group for comparison. Overall evidence is weak for podcasts as educational tools. However, the same could be said for many traditional teaching techniques in medicine.
cells.note: The review synthesized 11 learning-outcome articles with heterogeneous designs and comparisons; timing was not uniform, although the reported assessments generally followed the intervention.

cells.quote: Quitadamo et al. [38] showed that physicians were found to prescribe fewer proton pump inhibitors after utilizing the podcast than prior to the podcast. However, the extent of the behavior change correlated to the podcast was not statistically significant when compared to conventional training via written synopses [38].
cells.note: The review reports one behavioral-outcome study; no study design details or effect size are provided in the study text.
